figures.caption: Tē 99 tô.—Kēng-chek-chhé kap sîn-keng ê kun kúi-nā ê tô: A, chiū-sī tùi thâu-chêng kā i khòaⁿ, tī chia sîn-keng ê chêng-kun ū koah tng (chiàⁿ-pêng); B, tùi chiàⁿ-pêng-piⁿ kā i khòaⁿ; C, téng-bīn hoâiⁿ-tng-bīn; D, sîn-keng kun kap sîn-keng-chat tùi ē-bīn kā i khòaⁿ: 1, chêng-chhiòng-lia̍t; 2, āu-chhiòng-lia̍t; 3, chêng-kun teh chhut ê pō͘-ūi; 4, āu-kun teh jip ê pō͘-ūi; 5, chêng-kun; 5′, A, chêng-kun koah-tng; 6, āu-kun, i-ê chhiam-î teh jip 6′, chiū-sī sîn-keng-chat; 7, sîn-keng ê chêng-chi; 7′, sîn-keng ê hō͘-chi. (Allen Thomson, from Lewis' “Anatomy and Physiology for Nurses,” by permission of W. B. Saunders Co., publishers.)
